old_description: L3Harris Power Paragon designs and manufactures engineered power distribution solutions. Specialty is custom switchgear – including low-, medium-, and high-voltage switchgear, DC power systems and automated transfer switchgear – for commercial, utility and government power systems.
about: L3Harris Power Paragon is based in Anaheim, California, and operates under the L3Harris Technologies brand, with its web presence hosted at l3harris.com. The division designs and manufactures engineered power distribution solutions, with a specialty in custom switchgear. Its product line includes custom low-voltage and medium-voltage switchgear, power distribution control centers, automatic transfer switchgear (including paralleling systems), DC switchgear and bus systems, and high-voltage switchgear. These products are engineered for integration into complex power distribution networks. The company serves four primary industry segments: commercial construction, where its switchgear is installed in building power systems; utility and power generation, where equipment supports substation and grid distribution; government and military, meeting defense and federal facility requirements; and data centers, providing reliable power distribution for critical IT infrastructure.

about:
LA Packaging, based in Yorba Linda, California, was founded in 1984 by Edward Loritz Sr. with a commitment to supplying American-made hinged-lid plastic containers at affordable prices. The company continues his legacy, manufacturing its product lines domestically using medical-grade, Class VI polypropylene that meets REACH, RoHS, and FDA requirements.

The firm specializes in injection-molded clarified polypropylene, polyethylene, and ESD-safe containers and vials, offering customization through hot stamping and custom labeling. Its production capabilities have expanded to serve customers across North America, Europe, and Asia, with all manufacturing performed in the United States.

LA Packaging serves the electronic, medical, pharmaceutical, industrial, food, and laboratory sectors. It also operates two direct-to-customer e-commerce sites: lacontainerstore.com for bulk orders and esdplasticcontainers.com for small-quantity, no-minimum purchases of ESD-inhibiting containers.

The company differentiates itself by using higher-cost, medical-grade polypropylene that avoids harmful chemicals and leaching, and by providing personalized service including Net 30 terms and direct phone support.

name: LC Fine Foods
old_description: LC Cash and Carry, also known as LC Fine Food, is an establishment steeped in history, founded by the late and great Italo “Leo” Ciocca in the year 1965. Leo’s vision was to offer the finest Italian imports to his esteemed clientele. With his unwavering commitment to excellence and his unbridled passion for the food industry, Leo expanded his business, reaching new heights of success, while simultaneously adding new products and acquiring new customers across the wholesale and retail sectors. Today, his legacy lives on through LC Cash and Carry, where the tradition of offering authentic Italian products still remains strong, while at the same time, embracing the evolution of the market by adding a vast assortment of domestic products to cater to a wider audience.
about:
LC Fine Foods, operating as LC Cash and Carry, has been a fixture in New Haven, Connecticut since 1965. The company was founded by Italian immigrant Italo “Leo” Ciocca, who envisioned bringing the finest Italian imports to his community. What began as a modest enterprise grew steadily through Leo’s commitment to quality and service, establishing a reputation in the wholesale food trade.

Today the business functions as both a wholesale distributor and a cash-and-carry retailer, stocking a wide range of Italian and domestic food products. Its offerings span fresh produce, deli items, groceries, pasta, oils, cheeses, bakery goods, coffee, and seasonal specialties. The remodeled New Haven store serves walk-in customers six days a week, while a delivery operation supplies restaurants, delis, and institutions across the region.

The customer base includes independent restaurants, delicatessens, institutional kitchens, and retail shoppers. A deli owner in New Haven County describes the company as a primary supplier for fresh produce and cold cuts, while home cooks rely on it for traditional ingredients like San Marzano tomatoes and panettone. The firm also works with domestic and international suppliers, emphasizing relationships with local farmers and dairy producers.

The Ciocca family’s second generation, Carlo and Danny, now lead the company after Leo’s passing in 2023. They cite their differentiators as a family-owned legacy, direct supplier relationships, a commitment to local sourcing, and a service model that blends wholesale efficiency with retail accessibility.

name: LGC Clinical Diagnostics (Maine Standards)
old_description: Maine Standards is a market leader for linearity and calibration verification products. Our modern laboratory and streamlined processes allow us to consistently manufacture products that are of the highest quality, are easy-to-use and are incredibly efficient.
about:
LGC Maine Standards operates from Cumberland Foreside, Maine. The business traces its lineage to Maine Standards Company, LLC, which was acquired by LGC in November 2015 and rebranded as LGC Maine Standards. LGC itself dates back to 1842 as the UK Government Chemist and was privatized in 1996; it is now owned by funds affiliated with KKR. No individual founders are named in the company’s public materials.

The company manufactures linearity and calibration verification products, most notably the VALIDATE® line of liquid, ready‑to‑use, multi‑level sets configured for widely used clinical instruments. Production takes place in a modern laboratory using streamlined processes, and the firm emphasizes a global logistics network that ships on the customer’s schedule. LGC’s broader operations employ over 2,000 people across 22 countries, though headcount for the Maine site is not disclosed.

Primary customers are clinical laboratories in the diagnostics sector, but LGC’s measurement products and services also serve pharmaceuticals, agricultural biotechnology, food, environment, government, and academia. The VALIDATE® configurations are designed for the most widely used instruments in clinical chemistry, immunology, and hematology testing.

Maine Standards states that its 100 % satisfaction guarantee reflects more than 100 years of combined experience in linearity and calibration verification. The company’s stated purpose is to improve the quality of human diagnostics, and it adheres to the AdvaMed Code of Ethics for interactions with healthcare professionals.

name: LGND ENERGY
old_description: Your home is one of the biggest investments you will ever make. Utilizing solar energy will help improve the value of a home while giving you benefits while living in the home. Solar panels from LGND Energy are of the highest quality on the market in New Mexico. We have been working to provide roofing and solar solutions for homeowners for many years. Using solar energy gives you the freedom to control your power production, lower your energy bill, and help improve the environment.
about:
LGND Energy was founded in 2019 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, by brothers Elmer and Octavio Reyna. After years sales teams at larger solar firms, the pair wanted to bring a family-oriented culture to both their representatives and customers, so they launched their own solar sales dealership with a mission to pass savings directly to homeowners.

The company designs, sells, and installs residential and commercial photovoltaic systems across Albuquerque and Bernalillo County. Its services include roof consultations to verify structural readiness, full permitting and HOA coordination, and battery-backup installation using Tesla Powerwall 3 and Enphase units. Field crews, often including father-and-son teams, also fit critter guards and clean arrays.

LGND serves homeowners, small and large businesses, and multi-family properties throughout central New Mexico. Reviews cite projects ranging from single-family rooftops to commercial arrays, with the team managing city permits and utility interconnection on the customer's behalf.

The founders frame their differentiation around a low-pressure sales model: representatives complete extensive training and are compensated to prioritize customer fit over volume. The brothers started the business to reward reps for hard work while delivering the “family feel” they missed at prior employers.

We love bringing your big ideas to life, whether you need tables and chairs for your business or restaurant, or you want to invest in a specialized dining set for your home.
about:
LIW Furniture operates from East Earl in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The family-owned business is led by Case Taylor, who brought hands-on experience from Amish Artisan Woodcraft into the venture. Taylor's background in cabinetry, millwork, and custom furniture shaped the company's focus on practical design and durable construction.

The shop produces custom hardwood and iron furniture — dining tables, chairs, cabinets, office pieces, and specialty items — all hand crafted on site. Materials are sourced from native Appalachian forests, giving the team control over lumber selection through local partnerships. Customers choose from a catalogue of solid-wood designs or collaborate with in-house designers and craftsmen to specify finishes, hardware, and live-edge tops with custom bases.

LIW serves both residential and commercial clients. Restaurants, retail spaces, and offices have commissioned dining sets, built-ins, vanities, and bar installations; a restaurant project for John Harris is cited as a reference. The company also works with homeowners on dining-room collections and one-off pieces.

The company emphasizes that it never sacrifices quality for quantity, maintaining oversight from raw lumber to final finish. Its differentiators include locally sourced hardwoods, hand-crafted construction in a Lancaster wood shop, and a design process that lets customers tailor stains, paints, metal features, and live-edge details to exact specifications.

about:
LQ Mechatronics is based in Branford, Connecticut. The company operates as a system supplier for electromechanical complete solutions, focusing on control and installation technology for machine and plant engineering. While its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, the business has been a member of the Packaging Valley network since 2016.

The company designs and manufactures modular control cabinets, energy guidance systems, and custom cable assemblies. Using a standardized modular principle called the EnergyLink system, LQ combines round connectors, power cables, distributors, and functional modules into ready-to-install units. The firm reports 365 specialists across three locations, producing 305,000 systems and 2,990 kilometers of cable annually. Capabilities extend to pre-assembled energy chains, A-TEC functional modules for decentralized mounting, and full engineering, logistics, and on-site service support.

LQ serves primarily the machine building, plant engineering, and automation sectors, with a noted presence in the packaging industry through its Packaging Valley membership. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and system integrators seeking to reduce interface complexity in motion control and power distribution installations.

The company emphasizes complexity reduction through its modular building-block approach, which aims to eliminate interface problems and accelerate processes from engineering through logistics to assembly. It differentiates itself with 100% tested quality on all cable assemblies and claims industry-standard-setting pre-assembled energy chains.

name: Laguna Fabrics
old_description: Since 2000, Laguna has been making fabric with raw materials that have a lower environmental impact than conventional materials and today we are doing even more.
about:
Laguna Fabrics was founded in 1986 in Los Angeles, California, by Monet Goode and has been operated by the Roshan family across multiple generations. The family-owned company began as a circular knit mill serving the contemporary fashion market.

The company produces sustainable circular knit fabrics using in-house knitting machines ranging from low to fine gauge, with a capacity of 1.5 million pounds per month. Its 40-person team handles fabric development, technical analysis, new construction engineering, and sample yardage production. Special finishes include brushing, sueding, and fabric laundering, supported by a multi-layer quality control protocol and an on-site knitting technician.

Laguna serves contemporary fashion brands, young designers, and start-ups seeking sustainable domestic textiles. Longtime clients rely on the mill's quick turnaround and in-stock natural fiber yarns such as GOTS-certified organic cotton, TENCEL™ lyocell and modal, recycled cotton, and hemp.

Since 2000, Laguna has prioritized lower-impact materials, and in 2019 became the only circular knit mill in the United States with GOTS certification. The company's stated goal is to reach 90% sustainable material output by 2025, guided by core values of provenance, process transparency, and product authenticity.

name: Lakeland Engineering Equipment Company - Kansas City
old_description: Delta Fabricating designs and manufactures a variety of enclosures to protect your sophisticated electrical and electronic controls, instruments, and components from water, dust, dirt, oil and other environmental conditions. Delta Fabricating specializes in custom enclosures and panels to fit the needs of many industrial and commercial applications while providing quick delivery times.
about:
Lakeland Engineering Equipment Company was founded in 1952 by Bill Fox in Minneapolis, Minnesota, as a family-owned distributor of process motor controls and electrical components. The business has since grown into an international enterprise with offices in four states, including a Kansas City, Kansas location that serves as a regional hub.

The company distributes a vast inventory of electrical control components, solenoid valves, drives, switches, process motor controls, PLCs, HMIs, and explosion-proof parts from over 100 approved manufacturers. Beyond distribution, Lakeland provides engineering services, rents electrical test and power monitoring equipment, manages customer inventory to prevent supply-chain disruptions, and fabricates custom electrical enclosures through its Delta Fabricating division.

Lakeland serves industrial and commercial customers who rely on electrical controls, instrumentation, and component protection. Its clients include operations that need reliable component supply, custom enclosure solutions, and rental equipment for quality monitoring and power testing.

Since its founding, Lakeland has operated on the principle that customers should never have to choose between quality components, excellent service, and fast delivery. The company differentiates itself through its approved distributor status for more than 100 manufacturers, multi-location support across the Midwest and Mountain West, and an integrated service model that combines distribution, fabrication, rentals, and inventory management.

name: Lakeside Steel Manufacturing Co
old_description: Lakeside Steel & Mfg. Co. has served the metal fabrication needs for the power generation industry, material handling, construction equipment, and original equipment manufacturers for over 100 years. We use our experience, creativity, imagination, and best manufacturing principles to make the impossible possible for our customers.
about:
Lakeside Steel & Mfg. Co. operates from Kenosha, Wisconsin, where it has provided metal fabrication services for more than a century. The company’s history spans over 100 years, though a specific founding year is not publicly documented. Ownership details and founder names have not been disclosed.

The shop runs a 41,000-square-foot fabrication facility supported by an 11,000-square-foot warehouse that stocks carbon and stainless steel sheet, plate, and structural shapes. In-house processes include CNC plasma and flame cutting, shearing, press braking, plate rolling, welding, and painting, while stress relieving, blast cleaning, galvanizing, machining, and non‑destructive testing are handled by qualified subcontractors. The plant is equipped with five overhead cranes (5–20 ton), eight jib cranes, a 600‑ton hydraulic press brake, plate rolls capable of 1‑inch thick plate, and 22 welding stations. Lakeside has produced single pieces as large as 13‑foot‑6‑inch diameter by 70‑foot long weighing over 105,000 pounds, and operates on multiple shifts to meet short lead times.

Primary markets are power generation, material handling, construction equipment, and original equipment manufacturers. Representative projects include combustors, air piping, coal ducts, trommels, inlet water pipes, forklift booms, shaker conveyors, fly ash silos, cement hoppers, explosion‑door components, galvanized platforms, and a variety of structural frames and enclosures.

Lakeside emphasizes its strategic location midway between Chicago and Milwaukee, which provides rapid highway and rail access for nationwide shipping. The company also highlights its on‑site steel inventory, multi‑shift staffing, and certified craftsmen as key factors that enable precise, timely delivery.
